desc:
Round the integer n to k significant digits. Keep the k leading digits of n and replace every digit after them with a zero. When the first dropped part is exactly half of the rounding unit, round away from zero.

Return the rounded integer. Zero stays zero.

n = 123456, k = 2  -> 120000
n = 995, k = 2     -> 1000
n = -4567, k = 1   -> -5000
n = 125, k = 2     -> 130
n = 7, k = 3       -> 7
hints: Count the digits of |n|. If there are at most k of them, nothing changes. Otherwise the digits to drop are the last digits - k ones.
Let p = 10digits - k. Then |n| // p is the kept part and |n| % p is the dropped part, which is compared with p / 2.
Round the magnitude with (|n| + p // 2) // p * p, which rounds halves up. Then reapply the sign. Carries are automatic: 995 rounds to 1000.
editorial: Only the magnitude matters for the digits, so work with a = |n| and restore the sign at the end. Let d be the number of digits of a. If d ≤ k, the number already has at most k significant digits and is returned unchanged.

Otherwise let p = 10d - k. Adding p // 2 before the integer division by p rounds half up: a remainder of at least p / 2 carries into the kept digits. Since d - k ≥ 1, the value p is even, so p // 2 is exact. A carry that overflows the digit count, such as 995 to 1000, still gives the right answer, because the result is still a multiple of p and has the right number of significant digits.
